content.content:
The provided page content doesn't include the detailed entries for `aws:ViaAWSMCPService` or `aws:CalledViaAWSMCP`. The content is truncated before the request-properties section, so I can't quote their descriptions, data types, values, or availability.

The only reference is in the summary table under "Properties of the request," which lists them alongside `aws:ViaAWSService` and `aws:CalledVia`, plus a related key, `aws:IsMcpServiceAction`. The page also mentions AWS MCP Server in the `aws:SignInSessionArn` section, but doesn't describe these keys.

To get the exact details, check the full "AWS global condition context keys" page in the IAM User Guide (`reference_policies_condition-keys.html`), in the request-properties section.

[WebFetch note: this page's text is 164011 characters long and the answer above covers only characters 0 to 100000; the final 64011 were not read — to read on, call WebFetch again with the same url and offset: 100000.]
Yes, Required reviewers supports **Prevent self-review**. It stops users from approving workflow runs they triggered. The maximum is **6 people or teams** per environment.

Yes, `serverless package` exists. According to the page, it "packages your entire infrastructure into the `.serverless` directory by default." You can change the output location with the `--package` option.

The page doesn't mention a change set, diff, or noDeploy feature, so I can't confirm whether any of them exist.

When a job references an environment, the `sub` claim uses this format:

`repo:ORG-NAME/REPO-NAME:environment:ENVIRONMENT-NAME`

For example, a job in the `octo-repo` repository owned by `octo-org`, referencing an environment named `Production`, produces:

`repo:octo-org/octo-repo:environment:Production`

If the environment name contains a colon, the colon is replaced with `%3A`. An environment named `Production:V1` produces `repo:octo-org/octo-repo:environment:Production%3AV1`.

For repositories using immutable subject claims, the page's immutable syntax adds owner and repository IDs to the `repo` segment. The page doesn't show an environment-specific immutable example, but applying the same pattern would give `repo:OWNER@OWNER-ID/REPO@REPO-ID:environment:ENVIRONMENT-NAME`.

The exact name is **"Require approval of the most recent reviewable push."**

The page doesn't describe this setting in detail. It appears only in a note under **Require a pull request before merging > Additional settings**. The note says that if this setting is selected along with **Dismiss stale pull request approvals when new commits are pushed**, manually creating a pull request's merge commit and pushing it directly to a protected branch will fail unless the merge's contents exactly match the merge GitHub generates.

**Enforcement levels** (set per policy, and overridable per policy group):

- **Advisory:** warns about the violation without blocking the deployment.
- **Mandatory:** blocks the deployment.
- **Remediate:** fixes the violation automatically.
- **Disabled:** turns the policy off.

**Running a pack locally:** Use `pulumi preview --policy-pack` to test a custom policy pack on your machine before publishing it to Pulumi Cloud.

**Features requiring a paid edition:**

- **Essentials edition and above:** the Pulumi Best Practices and AWS Organizations Tag Policies pre-built packs.
- **Enterprise edition:** the compliance-framework pre-built packs, including CIS, PCI DSS, HITRUST, NIST, ISO 27001, and CMMC.

The page doesn't cover most of these topics:

- **Slack integration:** Not mentioned. The page says TEAM provides "Automatic notification of TEAM request, approval and session status" but doesn't name Slack or say whether notifications are one-way or support approvals.
- **Approvers:** The page says "Approvers can review requests before deciding whether to grant access," but doesn't describe how approvers are assigned.
- **Approver groups:** Not addressed.
- **Max duration:** Not specified. The page says access is time-bound and is removed automatically once the period ends.
- **Auto-approval:** Not mentioned. The described workflow includes an approver review before access is granted.

content.content:
**Approval workflow**

- **Where approvals happen:** Approvers log in to the TEAM application to approve or reject elevated access requests. The page does not describe approving through other channels.
- **Who approves:** Approver groups are defined by an approval policy that an admin creates. Admins use these policies to delegate approval for specific accounts and Organizational Units.
- **Notifications:** After a requester submits a request, the approver group is notified. The requester is notified when the request is approved and again when the access becomes active. The page does not describe the notification channels. It refers to a separate notification configuration guide.
- **Multiple approvers:** The page says a *group* of approvers is notified, but it does not say whether one approver or all of them must approve.
- **Auto-approval:** The page does not mention auto-approval.
- **Approver restrictions:** Approvers can request elevated access, but they cannot approve or reject their own requests.
- **Approver visibility:** Approvers can view historical details and session logs for requests within the scope they are authorized to approve.

**Slack notifications:** The settings page includes a "Send Slack notifications" toggle that enables or disables Slack notifications. If you turn it on, you must also enter a **Slack OAuth token**, which gives TEAM permission to your Slack workspace as a bot user.

**Can approvals be done via Slack?** The page doesn't say. It only describes Slack as a notification channel, so don't assume approvals can be actioned from Slack.

**Notification channels:**
- **Amazon SES (email):** Enabled with "Send email notifications." You must set a **Source email**. The optional **Source ARN** is needed only if the SES identity is in a different AWS account than the TEAM deployment account.
- **Amazon SNS:** Enabled with "Send SNS notifications."
- **Slack:** Enabled with "Send Slack notifications," plus the OAuth token above.

**Approval workflow settings:**
- **Approval workflow** (global toggle): Determines whether eligibility policies can require approval. If disabled, eligible requesters don't need approval. The "Approval required" setting on individual eligibility policies is ignored in that case.
- **Request expiry timeout:** Sets how long a request stays pending before it expires and must be resubmitted. The default is 3 hours.

Based only on this page:

- **Approval required toggle:** This sets whether elevated access requested under the policy needs approval. The page doesn't explicitly say that turning it off means automatic approval. It also notes the setting can be turned off globally in TEAM settings.
- **Max duration:** Set in hours, from 1 to 8,000 (about one year).
- **Approver policy groups:** These aren't fields of an eligibility policy. They belong to separate approval policies, each with one or more IAM Identity Center groups, scoped to an account or OU. If an eligibility policy requires approval for an account and no approval policy covers that account (or its groups have no members), users can't request access to it.
- **Multiple approvers:** An approval policy can list one or more groups, but the page doesn't say how many approvals a single request requires.
- **Slack mention:** The page doesn't mention Slack.
